title: Say Any Word 20 Times and It Stops Making Sense

scenes.text: Say the word spoon out loud twenty times. Go on, try it.
Somewhere around repeat ten, it stops sounding like a word. It's just a weird noise.
Psychologists call it semantic satiation. The name was coined in nineteen sixty-two at McGill University.
In lab tests, people who repeated a word got slower at tasks that used its meaning, like sorting it into a category.
It happens because the connection between a word's sound and its meaning weakens, a little more, every time you fire it.
Pick a word and try it right now. Which one broke first for you?
